title: Chapter 4: Surprise Reward
html:
One of the bathroom windows must have been open, because a cold draft drifted through the room, brushing across Chen Ge’s face like an invisible hand.

The cubicle doors creaked as the wind nudged them back and forth. Drops of water gathered near the corner of the ceiling and fell to the floor, sending insects skittering away. Every tiny sound made Chen Ge imagine something crawling across his skin.

The surrounding silence magnified every noise, enough to make most people anxious. Chen Ge, however, had been hardening his nerves since childhood, and his response to fear was somewhat duller than normal.

He emptied his mind and focused on counting down the time.

About twenty minutes had passed when, for no apparent reason, the room began to grow colder. It felt as though blocks of ice had been placed all around him, and he shivered involuntarily.

Stay calm! Don’t overthink it and scare yourself! Only ten minutes left. Chen Ge, you can do this!A strange current of air circled beside his ear, as though something were moving around him. He clenched his fists so tightly that the veins stood out on the backs of his hands, yet the rest of his body seemed petrified.

“Chen Ge, Chen Ge, Chen Ge…”

He continued murmuring his name. With only five minutes remaining, Chen Ge sensed the candlelight die away, and another presence in the darkness seemed to call his name.

Echo? Impossible!

“Chen Ge…” The voice seemed to be calling to him with growing urgency, as though it had something crucial to say.

The voice seems to be coming from outside the door. Should I go take a look?However, Chen Ge quickly dismissed the thought. The rules were explicit: he had to remain in front of the mirror and do nothing else.

He continued the countdown in his head as the voice beside him began to distort. By now, he was certain someone else was calling his name—and that person was standing outside the bathroom door.

They sound so urgent, but I’m the one playing this game. Why are they in such a hurry? This is obviously a trap. What a cheap trick.Chen Ge curled his lip in disdain. The setup and atmosphere are good, but the scare itself is too obvious and straightforward.

During the final three minutes, a shrill scraping came from the bathroom door, as though someone were raking their fingernails across it—or gnawing at it with their teeth. The door gave a faint creak, as if it might open at any moment.

1,798 seconds, 1,799 seconds, 1,800 seconds!The half-hour limit was up. Every sound vanished at once, and silence returned.

To make sure he had not miscounted, Chen Ge kept his eyes shut and counted another three hundred beats. Only then did he step back, place both hands over his chest, and open his eyes.

The candle had gone out, leaving the bathroom in darkness. For some reason, Chen Ge sensed that something had changed. He switched on the flashlight, and when light once again filled the cramped room, he froze.

The mirror before him was covered in cracks, splitting his reflection into countless fragments. The effect was dizzying, but what frightened him more was the broken doll sitting in front of the mirror.

Its button eyes gleamed, and its patchwork body was stuffed with cotton. The doll was old, but it held special meaning for Chen Ge: it was the very first toy he had made, and it had been found at the scene of his parents’ disappearance.

The doll leaned against the mirror as though it were trying to keep whatever was inside from coming out.

“Wait. The bathroom door was locked, so how did you get in? Through the window? No—the bigger question is how you moved on your own!” Chen Ge felt as though his world were coming apart and needed several minutes to process what he was seeing. He and the doll stared at each other for nearly three minutes before he finally recovered. Flexing his cold fingers, he slowly approached it.

For some reason, the doll’s button eyes seemed to follow him. Chen Ge’s lips twitched as he looked at his creation. Giving the doll a wide berth, he reached for the phone beside it. “Good thing I had the sense to prepare for this.”

The phone had finished recording. Chen Ge made a backup copy before reviewing the footage.

The video quality was poor. The lone candle flame danced in the darkness, and while the real Chen Ge looked tense in front of the mirror, his reflection seemed strangely relaxed.

The first ten minutes were uneventful, but things began to change around the eleven-minute mark.

The phone had not captured the wind, but the video clearly showed the cubicle door moving.

Then white noise interrupted the footage. Nothing in the video was more than slightly unusual, yet for some reason it was deeply unsettling. Perhaps that was simply humanity’s instinctive fear of darkness and the unknown.

As the video continued, Chen Ge’s face grew paler. He remembered clearly that he had not moved while his eyes were closed, yet in the recording his body slowly leaned forward, as though trying to enter the mirror.

By the twenty-five-minute mark, his upper body was bent forward at nearly seventy degrees, the tip of his nose almost touching the mirror.

Several seconds later, without warning, spidery cracks began spreading across the mirror. Even Chen Ge’s heart skipped a beat. Then something even more unbelievable happened: the expression on his reflection changed. It grinned wickedly and began pounding frantically against the glass.

At that exact moment, the candle went out and the video ended.

Because of the camera angle, the footage showed nothing involving the doll, and Chen Ge had no idea what had happened during those final five minutes.

“From the looks of it, the thing in the mirror wanted to get out, but this doll stopped it. Does that mean the doll saved me?” Chen Ge picked it up from the counter and asked seriously, “Can you understand me? Do you know what happened to my parents?”

Naturally, the doll did not answer, though its button eyes seemed to gleam in the darkness.

Cradling the doll in his arms, he turned toward the bathroom door. Still unwilling to step outside, he crouched beneath one of the windows and pulled out his phone. A mission-completion message was waiting for him.

“You were extraordinarily lucky. Congratulations on completing the Nightmare Mission! Mission Reward Obtained—Elementary Skill: Mortician’s Makeup.

“Mortician’s Makeup: I hope you will treat this talent with the respect it deserves. Unlike ordinary beauty makeup, a mortician works only with the dead. Your hands can breathe life into lifeless faces, granting them a final, enduring beauty.

“First Nightmare Mission completed. Title unlocked: Newcomer of Nightmare Town. Additional reward obtained: Trial Mission unlocked for the 1-Star scenario Murder by Midnight! Complete the Trial Mission to add this scenario to your Haunted House!”

Reading the messages on the screen, Chen Ge realized just how important a skilled makeup artist could be to a Haunted House. Actors and props alike depended on makeup to bring them to life, and convincing effects could dramatically increase a scenario’s scare factor.
